10.1002_adfm.78458: Built‐in electric field (BIEF) engineering has emerged as a promising strategy for regulating interface electron structure and tailoring multifunctional performance; however, constructing strong BIEF to achieve multifunctionality remains a challenge. Herein, an intensified‐BIEF strategy through nitrogen configuration regulation is proposed in CoNi/Mo 2 C@N‐doped carbon (NC) composites to simultaneously enhance electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption and anti‐corrosion. By tailoring pyrolysis temperature, the nitrogen configuration and electronic structure of the NC matrix are systematically regulated, enlarging the work function difference and strengthening BIEF at the CoNi/NC and NC/Mo 2 C heterointerfaces. The intensified BIEF induces directional charge migration, generating oriented interface dipole arrays that enhance the dipole‐array polarization relaxation and boost conductive loss. Meanwhile, the strong BIEF facilitates electron accumulation at the CoNi surface, suppressing charge delocalization that inhibits anodic dissolution and promotes passivation. The optimized CoNi/Mo 2 C@NC achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 6 GHz at a thickness of 1.8 mm. Meanwhile, compared with commercial absorbers, the corrosion potential is increased by 94.9%, while the corrosion current is reduced by 74.5%, demonstrating exceptional durability and ultralow corrosion kinetics in marine environments. This work reveals the mechanistic role of strong BIEF in simultaneously optimizing EMW absorption and anti‐corrosion, and provides a novel strategy for designing multifunctional materials.
10.1016_j.nanoen.2026.112275: With the accelerating demand for critical minerals and the imminent surge of end-of-life lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), efficient recycling technologies are urgently needed to secure a sustainable resource supply and enable a circular battery economy. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) offer an environmentally benign pathway for metal recovery, yet their practical implementation is constrained by inherently slow leaching rates. In this study, microwave-responsive DESs were rationally designed using choline chloride as a common, low-cost hydrogen-bond acceptor, while varying the hydrogen-bond donor to tune acidity, metal coordination, and leaching performance. Among the DESs investigated, choline chloride-lactic acid delivered the highest metal recovery, achieving >99% extraction of Co and Mn and >92% extraction of Li and Ni from industrial LIB black mass within only 30 min at 200 °C under microwave irradiation. The exceptional performance is attributed to rapid volumetric heating and enhanced solvent-solid interactions, which accelerate mass transfer and metal dissolution. Combined spectroscopic and thermal analyses revealed a ligand-assisted leaching mechanism involving proton-mediated metal-oxygen bond cleavage and stabilization of dissolved metal species through chloride-lactate coordination. The DES maintained high leaching efficiency over multiple recycling cycles and enabled downstream metal separation via selective precipitation. Life cycle assessment confirmed the environmental viability of the process and identified energy consumption as the primary hotspot for future optimization. This study establishes a rapid, energy-efficient, and environmentally benign microwave-assisted solvo-metallurgical strategy for the sustainable recovery of critical metals from spent LIBs.
10.1021_acs.jpclett.5c03896: Geometric tuning of supports is an emerging strategy to optimize catalysts, yet its role in governing the synergy of heteronuclear p–d dual-atom catalysts (DACs) is unexplored. Using carbon nanotubes (CNTs) as tunable curvature substrates, we investigated their influence on SiFeN 6 DACs via first-principles calculations. We reveal an inverted-volcano-type relationship between curvature and activity, originating from the nonlinear differential response of key intermediates. This curvature-driven trend is a general principle applicable to other 3d transition metals (TM = Mn, Co, Ni). To rationalize this complex relationship, we integrated a machine learning (SISSO) approach, which yielded a robust multidimensional descriptor ( R 2 = 0.92). By quantitatively revealing the dominant role of the p-block Si site, our data-driven model establishes substrate geometry as a primary and effective design strategy for optimizing these complex dual-atom catalysts.
10.1021_acsami.6c12360: Printed electrochemical sensors offer a promising route toward decentralized diagnostics and environmental monitoring, but their practical use remains constrained by complex electrode fabrication and instrument-dependent readout. Here, we present a tap-to-detect sensing platform that couples digitally printed gold nanoparticle nanoelectronics with a battery-free near-field communication (NFC) potentiostat. Single-pass digital materials deposition enables direct fabrication of ready-to-use AuNP working/counter electrodes and AgNP reference electrodes on a flexible polyimide substrate, producing mechanically robust and electrochemically reliable devices. The NFC potentiostat provides smartphone-based wireless voltammetric readout with performance comparable to a commercial potentiostat. As proof of versatility, the printed AuNP electrode is applied to two distinct sensing modes: the thiol-mediated aptamer functionalization enables label-free HER2 biosensing with a detection limit of 4.87 pg mL-1 and successful analysis in spiked human serum, while the intrinsic Au-As interaction enables direct As(III) detection with a detection limit of 42.5 ng mL-1, without additional electrode modification. This digitally printed, smartphone-readable gold nanoelectronic platform provides a scalable pathway toward portable electrochemical sensing for healthcare and environmental applications.
10.1021_jacsau.6c01196: Skeletal editing has emerged as a transformative strategy for the direct remodeling of molecular frameworks through selective atom insertion, deletion, or exchange. Through structural remodeling at the molecular core, skeletal editing provides rapid access to diverse and valuable architectures while circumventing lengthy de novo or multistep synthetic routes. In recent years, the merger of skeletal editing and electrochemistry has unlocked entirely new opportunities for sustainable and programmable molecular editing. Thus, protons and electrons serve as traceless redox reagents, enabling distinct reaction manifolds compared with conventional thermal approaches. Moreover, electrochemical activation offers unique advantages, including tunable redox control, reduced chemical waste, and access to reactive intermediates under mild reaction conditions. In this perspective, we highlight recent advances in electrochemical skeletal editing until September 2026, with particular emphasis on electrochemical atom insertion, ring expansion, and ring contraction strategies.
